Rio das Flores and its surroundings are included in journeys through the Coffee Valley. Historic coffee farms and estates have been preserved in this region and can be explored on guided excursions.

Visits to local plantations reveal the history of coffee production and life on the estates. The journey through the region can continue to other Coffee Valley estates and mountain areas.

Rio Frio Cave lies along the route through the Mountain Pine Ridge reserve in Belize. Travelers visit it on the way to Caracol, together with the Rio On natural pools.

A stop at the cave introduces the rock formations of this forested region. This combination allows a walk in nature to complement visits to Maya structures.

From the outside, the cathedral resembles a large concrete cone. Inside, the impression changes: vertical bands of stained glass rise toward the top of the building, and daylight fills the space with color. The circular floor plan makes the interior feel like one continuous hall.

Construction began in 1964, and the ceremonial consecration took place in 1979. The building was designed by architect Edgar de Oliveira da Fonseca. The church is dedicated to Saint Sebastian, the patron saint of Rio de Janeiro.

The cathedral features on itineraries through the city's central districts. This stop complements the exploration of colonial architecture: a major building from the second half of the 20th century stands near historic streets. Access to the interior depends on the itinerary and whether the cathedral is open.

The Rio On natural river pools in the Mountain Pine Ridge reserve feature on itineraries through mainland Belize. A visit is combined with Caracol and Rio Frio Cave.

After exploring the ancient Maya city, travelers stop here to rest and swim. Sections of river among the rocks provide a chance to spend part of the day by the water.
